- Level 5 on: leather armour from Hound and Skin-Stealer hides; then copper and bronze from Level 8.

guide-home-text:
Home and Expeditions
You only ever wake up in Level 0. Make it somewhere worth waking up.

The Backrooms are survived from a home, in expeditions. Everything that follows is built on one fact: however deep you go, when you die you wake in the Lobby, with nothing, and what you carried lies where you fell, in a level you cannot wake up in.

Where you wake
Where you woke is home until you move it; the map marks it as "Where I woke up". To move it, hold a temporal gear and rightmouse the floor anywhere in Level 0. Anywhere else it will not take hold (and is not used up). Gears are very rare: a sealed supply box holds one about once in a hundred, deep caches a little more often, and the prize counter of Level 3999 sells one for 200 tickets. Good places to call home: the Manila Room (nothing hostile goes in, and it steadies you), beside a way out you know, and beside a flooded room, for water.

Resting
The longer you are out without a rest, the bolder what lives here becomes (see What Lives Here); after ten in-game hours out, about twenty minutes of play, it is as bad as it gets. A rest is a full minute, without moving on, in any of these: within about 48 blocks of home in Level 0; beside a lit firepit or burning Firesalt (within 6 blocks); asleep in a bed; beside a wanderer; or in one of the safe places. A firepit and a chest halfway along a route you use make an outpost, and make it safe to stop.

What a home needs, and where it comes from
- Walls where you want them. Drywall and wallpaper break with any tool (an axe is quickest; bare hands take seven times as long) to join rooms or close off a corner. Concrete and floors take a copper pickaxe. To build, rubble masonry is 4 rubble in a 2 by 2, and rubble comes from breaking concrete and floor slabs with a copper pickaxe (about one rubble from two blocks), never from drywall. Beyond that, the usual vanilla blocks: cobblestone from Level 8's rock, bricks from clay. Only the roof of a level, and the top of the walls between levels, never give.
- A door. Nothing in the Backrooms opens doors, so a door is a wall to them. Planks come from Level 1's crates and pallets and Level 4's furniture.
- Storage. A chest (8 planks + 1 nails and strips, the nails from 2 metal brackets). Baskets need Level 10's cattails. Before that, most tools and many items can be stored on the ground.
- Light and fire. Torches on the walls, a firepit, Firesalt from Level 3 for when the lights fail. When a Reality Shift puts the lights out, eyes come to the edge of the dark even here; a door and a light keep them out.
- Cold storage. Level 0's blackout zones are cold and damp (10 °C): food in a chest there keeps more than twice as long as in the Lobby proper. See Food, Heat and Cold and the vanilla food preservation page.
- A farm. Soil comes from potted plants (Levels 4 and 5), the lawns of Levels 9, 10 and 11, or Level 94's turf; seeds from seed packets, Level 10's barns and wanderers; and water from a flooded room, a bucket, or a watering can, within 3 blocks of the farmland. Crops grow under a working ceiling light at a little over half the daylight pace, and hardly at all in the cold of the blackouts; plant under a lit troffer, not a dead one. See farming.
- A bed. The head end of a hotel bed (Level 5) comes away as a real bed you can sleep in; a hay bed is 3 hay from Level 10.

Food that comes back
Nothing in Levels 0 to 5 restocks except the Snackrooms' machines, Level 4's fountains and the Almond Water seeps and dispensers listed in Food, Heat and Cold. What does come back: fish (Level 7), game and berries (Level 9), crops, livestock and honey (Level 10), the iceboxes and milk vans of Level 94, and a farm of your own. Preserve with salt (Level 8's halite, ground in a quern) or a sealed crock.

Planning an expedition
- Rest first. Take four bags, a blade, a torch and a candle, Almond Water, food for the way back, a bandage, chalk if you have it, and any note you have not read yet (a note read in a new level tells of that level).
- Know the way back before you need it: every doorway between levels and every elevator, stairwell, door or pit you take is marked on your map the first time, with the way back where there is one (Ways Between Levels).
- The hot levels (2, 3, the boiler halls) burn food faster; the cold ones (6, 7's sea, 8, the Hub) want warm clothes.
- Leave an outpost on any route you mean to use twice.
guide-finding-text:
Finding the Way
Reaching the wall is not reaching the next level.

The map
Open it with worldmaphud. It shows only what you have actually seen: it fills in along your line of sight out to about 24 blocks, 4 in the dark (2 in Level 6), and remembers between sessions, so what you have mapped stays mapped. Walls block it. It marks "Where I woke up"; every doorway between levels you walk through and every elevator, stairwell, door or pit you take (with the way back where there is one); the places wanderers' notes tell of; chalk marks, in white; and sealed supply boxes and crates, in red. rightmouse the map to add waypoints of your own.
How much the map helps is chosen when a world is created (Backrooms map, under Survival challenges). With No waypoints it fills in just the same but marks nothing for you. With None there is no map or minimap at all: you find your way or you don't. Without waypoints, what would have been marked is told to you instead, as a direction and a number of paces, and your journal keeps what the notes said; chalk is how you find your way back, and with no map there is a little more of it in ceiling tiles and lost backpacks.

Gates
Where two levels meet the wall is solid, but every few hundred blocks along it there is a gate: two or three doorways side by side, each two blocks wide (in Level 1, under an EXIT sign). The first time you walk through one it is marked on your map. In Levels 0, 2 and 6 a hallway runs along the inside of the boundary wall: follow it and you will come to a gate, quietly, because the edge of a level is the most dangerous ground in it. The wall itself is not sacred below its roof line: a Level 0 boundary is papered drywall and breaks with any tool, a concrete one with a copper pickaxe, so with the right tool a wall is a slow way through rather than a dead end. Level 8 is solid rock, entered and left only where the 9th Road runs through it, and the open-sky levels (9, 10) have no wall between them at all.

Signs of a gate
- The doorway itself. Each level looks like itself right up to its wall; only the short passage through a gate shows the next level, with its doorway at the far end: Level 0's carpet worn to the concrete in the doorway to Level 1, the hotel's red carpet in Level 4's doorway to Level 5. (In worlds made before 0.514.0 the next level showed itself sooner: worn carpet and missing ceiling tiles near Level 1, pipes along Level 1's ceiling near Level 2, hotel red in Level 4's carpet near Level 5.)
- Chalk arrows on the walls, left by those who came before, point the way to the nearest gate from about a hundred blocks out (Levels 0 to 6). Chalk shows white on the map, so an arrow you have seen is a lead.
- Chalk crosses mean a dead end (most of the Lobby's blind hallways carry one), or, in a ring of them round a place with bones on the floor, a den: keep out.
- Facelings (the faceless people of Levels 1, 3, 4, 5 and 9): greet one with rightmouse and it waves, then turns and points toward the nearest gate it knows of within a few hundred blocks, and you are told which way it pointed and roughly how far.
- Wanderers' notes (rightmouse to read) mark a place on your map, by the paper: a note of a door marks the nearest gate (where there are no gates, the nearest way out); of a way, the nearest elevator, stairwell or pit; of something left, the nearest sealed box or crate; of a refuge, the nearest safe place or trader. The text tells you the direction and about how many paces. A note with nothing of its kind in range is handed back, to read somewhere else.

Notes and the journal
- What a note says is what the wanderers before you learned, and it comes in order. Whatever note you find first, it is the same first page anyone reads, and the next carries on from it. After the first three (the rules of the Lobby), notes take turns between the wanderers' way through the levels and what is known of the level you read them in. Some pages wait until you have been somewhere.
- Folded notes, taped small and written in ink, are rarer (deep caches, the hearts of dens, Red Rooms, rooms behind locked doors, lost backpacks, bedrolls, tents, the far edges of a level) and say something more exact: a route, the odds of a door, a rule that keeps you alive. What they mark, they find from twice as far, and show in gold.
- Every note marks somewhere new. A note never points at a place one of your earlier notes already marked while there is another to point at: the first supplies note marks the nearest unopened box, the next one the box after that, and so on outward; the same for gates, ways and refuges. Only when nothing else is in range does a note name a place again.
- A note is kept when read, and remembers who has read it: to you it is now "(read)", and reading it again only says so, but anyone else can read it for the next page in their sequence. One paper gives each player one read, so pass your notes on, or leave them where the next wanderer will find them.
- Notes stack by what they are about, 16 to a stack (a way through, a way out, supplies, a refuge; the folded notes together), so you can carry a bundle and read them where they will help, one at a time. Read notes stack apart from fresh ones.
- Some notes lie loose on the floor: at chalk-crossed dead ends, in the Manila Room and the Red Rooms, in Level 3's Sanctums and the Beverly Room, in the food courts, beside each arrival in Level !.
- Every note you read goes into your journal (journal, or .journal): the wanderers' way, a chapter for each level, the folded notes, and the directions you have been given, each with where you read it and, where the world has waypoints, Show on map and Mark again for what it marked. It is kept for you, not carried: dying loses nothing.
- You wake with a note already in your pocket: the first page, marking the nearest sealed box.
- Once you have read everything, a note is only its directions. Anything signed =) is a lie.

Ways through
Elevators, stairwells, doors, pits, vents and stranger things are the other ways between levels, often far shorter than walking. Two rules hold for all of them: a threshold always leads to the same place, and if you walked through it you can walk back (by the twin you come out beside, or by a thin spot left where you arrived), while if you fell, dived or were taken you cannot. Each is marked on your map the first time. The full list is Ways Between Levels.

Locked doors
Levels 1, 2, 4, 5 and 9 have rooms behind locked doors that nobody has been into since. A pry bar (2 metal brackets + 1 iron nails and strips; also found on tool shelves, in toolboxes and on workbenches; 24 uses) forces one in 4 seconds, for good, if there is a room behind it, and leaves you the door's bracket; everything near hears it. A door set in solid wall will not give, and a door that goes somewhere is not locked at all. The Lobby has no doors to force. Level 188's rooms open with its own keycards.

Expeditions
The longer you are out without resting, the more the Backrooms notice you (see Home and Expeditions for what counts as rest). Rest by a fire, beside a wanderer or in a safe place, then go on. Mark your way with chalk in the dark levels: choose arrow, cross or circle with the tool mode key (toolmodeselect), and rightmouse a wall; a mark can be changed by clicking it again (48 marks a stick). Chalk is made from a chalk stone, and falls out of ceiling tiles and lost backpacks now and then.

l974-mail-body:
Greetings, wanderer. If you are reading this, you picked up something cute on your travels, and Kitty liked it. Whatever you found is Kitty's now.

Kitty is the tall dark shape at the edge of your eye, the one that watches you sleep. It will not hurt you. You are its guest: do not hurt it, do not break its things, and try not to scream when it comes up behind you.

Kitty keeps the fridge and the cupboards full. Do not stay too long. The food turns to sugar, and the pink stops being kind.

When you want to leave, hold out the thing you brought and call: Here Kitty, Kitty, Kitty! It will take its gift, and you will wake somewhere just as safe.

note-m01:
Rule one: don't run. Nobody's coming, and running only brings the things that are. Rule two: break the boxes. Lid still taped down, there's food and Almond Water in it. Torn open, it's scraps. Rule three: keep any note you find. They turn up in order. Don't ask me how.
— Dez
note-m02:
You need an edge. Knock a dead light out of the ceiling for glass. A bare shard cuts, but it snaps one time in four. A shard, a strip of wallpaper and a carpet fibre make a shiv. A metal bracket, a strip and two fibres make a scraper, and that lasts three times as long. Either one peels clean, two to a cut. Keep it even once you've got flint.
— Dez
note-m03:
Blade in hand, right-click the yellow wallpaper, then the dry carpet. Strips and fibres. Two strips twist into dry grass. Three fibres make twine. Five fibres and a twine make a carpet bag, three slots. Make four before you go anywhere: that's thirty-two fibres, sixteen cuts with a shiv. The floor won't mind.
— Dez
note-m04:
Flint is rare in the boxes here; Level 1's crates and floors have it. With two: sneak, right-click one onto the floor, knap. Knife blade first, then an axe head, each hafted on a stick. One rotten wood (from the ceiling voids) gives two sticks; two give a firewood. Fire starter: one dry grass, two sticks. Firepit: dry grass on the floor, four firewood. Expect no wood here. Level 1 has wood.
— A.L., survey
note-m05:
Ruth, there's a little gear by my health that turns. Forward means this place has hold of me. Backward means I'm slipping, and when it empties it hurts. The dark rooms turn it back, and the red ones worst. A bottle of Almond Water gives back about a seventh. Every day or so the lights go out everywhere for hours. I stop, light a torch, drink if I must, and wait in a room I know. I think of you.
— Tom
note-m06:
Ruth, I died today. I woke up in the Lobby again with nothing; my things were still lying where I fell. It's always the Lobby. So I'm making a home. A temporal gear, used on the floor anywhere in this level, moves where you wake. Anywhere else it won't take. Fifty steps round home counts as rest. I've hung your photo by the door.
— Tom
note-m07:
This level is bounded. The wall at its edge is solid, with a gap every few hundred paces. Worn carpet and missing ceiling tiles mean you are close. A hallway runs along the inside of the wall: follow it, quietly; that is where they wait. Chalk arrows point to a gap; chalk crosses mean keep out. The nearest gap I surveyed is marked.
— A.L., survey
note-m08:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Eyes and a grin in a dark room: a Smiler. It will not enter firelight, and a candle is not fire enough. Carry a torch (two dry grass and a stick, lit at a fire). Hold its gaze, do not run, do not look away, and it stops. Running, breaking things open and long stays out all draw them. A minute beside a fire counts as rest.
— Field Team 9 (six of us)
note-m09:
First trip out is Level 1: a concrete car park in grey fog. Its wooden crates hold food, Almond Water, planks, twine and charcoal, and flint and stones lie loose on the floor. Eight planks and a nails and strips make a chest; two metal brackets make the nails. Bring planks home for a door. Nothing in here opens doors.
— Dez
note-m10:
Finding: the rings are only how it is built. Elevators, stairwells, doors and holes are the real map, and they are honest: each always leads to the same place. Walked through, it can be walked back, by the one you come out beside or by a thin spot, a pale seam in the air that hums. Fell or dived: no way back. Record every one.
— A.L., survey
note-m11:
Copper without a mine: cable spools, about four bits each (Levels 1 and 3); machine cabinets (Level 2); stacked pipes (Level 3), with lead. Twenty bits to an ingot; ten scrap wire to one. Melting wants a crucible and coal. Both are in Level 3.
— A.L., survey
note-m12:
Clay floors the flooded tunnels under Level 3: down a manhole. The water is freezing and the gear runs back faster there than anywhere I have measured, so dig and get out; the rungs go back up. Form a crucible, moulds, a pot and bowls, and fire them in a pit kiln. Coal is heaped by the generators.
— A.L., survey
note-m13:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Turn over the coal by Level 3's generators and Level 5's boilers for Firesalt. Set down, it burns for half a day and nothing hostile comes within eight paces. Salt and powdered sulfur make two. A lit firepit keeps Hounds off while it burns. A fire, a chest and some Firesalt halfway along a route make an outpost. Build them.
— Field Team 9 (five of us)
note-m14:
Cast a copper pickaxe and a hammer, and keep nine ingots for an anvil. Then break through any floor: eight blocks of concrete, and beneath it the ground of the world we came from. Rock, caves, ore, the better ores deeper. Prospect it as you would at home. Level 8 is that ground laid open, ore lying on the cave floors.
— A.L., survey
note-m15:
Level 4's the calmest place I know before the city. Grey carpet, fridges with fruit and cheese, Almond Water in the fountains and coolers. A few vending machines take you instead of serving you: you wake up in a food court and you can't walk back. Its stairwells sometimes come out in the Lobby. Learn one and you've got a road home.
— Dez
note-m16:
Level 5's got beds. Break the head end and it comes away whole: sleep in it at home. Linen off the foot end makes sacks, twine and linen, five slots. Clothes in the wardrobes and suitcases, silver off the silverware, brass off the luggage carts, coal in the boiler halls. The corridors get to you. The Beverly Room doesn't. Pell liked the hotel.
— Dez
note-m17:
Nothing grows unless you grow it, love. Seed packets turn up in tool shelves and kitchen cupboards, four seeds a packet. Soil comes out of the potted plants. Water within three steps: a flooded room in the dark zones, or a bucket. Plant under a working light, not a dead one; slower than sun, but it grows. The dark zones are cold, so food keeps there. My first turnip came up yesterday.
— Nell
note-m18:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Level 6 is dark. Not dim: dark. Your brightest light shows a few paces and your map forgets everything past arm's reach. Chalk the walls (right-click a wall; F chooses arrow, cross or circle): chalk stays, and shows on the map. Keep to the long dry corridors; the wet ones end blind. Follow the sound of waves to the stairs down. They are few, and deep in.
— Field Team 9 (four of us)
note-m19:
Level 7: water under a ceiling. Driftwood burns; fish bite. Depth costs light and steadiness, and something large circles at the edge of sight: if your gear fails down there, surface. A ring of standing stones: dive in the middle and you come up in the Suburbs. A cave mouth in the deep: the caves. Neither returns.
— A.L., survey
note-m20:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Level 8: stay on the 9th Road. Gravel, lamps, our waypoints, camps along it, Almond Water seeping from the rock beside it. Off it, drifters. All the ore is here: copper, tin, zinc, bismuth, gold, lead, coal and three kinds of iron. Halite grinds to salt in a quern. The vents beside the road go to Level 2 and back. Dress warm.
— Field Team 9 (three of us)
note-m21:
The Suburbs are always midnight, love. Search the houses: pantries, garages with tools and seeds, dressers of clothes. Behind some houses a path through a field ends at a gate, and the gate is Level 10: fields standing ripe, livestock, ponds, bee skeps, a quern in the barns. The old furrows are spent, so hoe fresh ground. Never dig below the soil there. I'm staying.
— Nell
note-m22:
In some of Level 10's barns a stretch of the east wall between the stalls isn't quite there. Walk into it. The city on the other side is safe, lit and stocked, with a door back to nearly everywhere: an apartment basement to the Lobby, a parking ramp to Level 1, a diner's kitchen to the food court. I've got a stall here now. Come and trade.
— Dez
note-m23:
Not every place lies on a ring. In the hotel, now and then, a locked door is cyan and reads POOL: warm water and white tile, where lit water heals you, but there is no food at all and the deep pits have no bottom I could find. In the Suburbs, a doll's house, too clean and too cream, opens on green hills where everything moves a frame at a time. Be indoors there by dusk.
— A.L., survey
note-m24:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. There is a place of tunnels and carved doors: the Hub. In by a grey door with a ring of marks over it, at the end of a maintenance hall in Level 1, chalk arrows leading to it; or one steel door in forty in Level 2, a chalk circle beside it. Most of its doors want a key, each its own level's, and the keys turn up in their own levels. A man in the Tower gives one away, once.
— Field Team 9 (two of us)
note-m25:
Ruth, I've stopped looking for the way out. Everything they wrote about the doors is true: each always goes to the same place, and a person could learn them all. Only none of them go back to you. If anyone finds a door that does, don't write it down. Just go. I'm going home now. Home is the Lobby.
— Tom
note-l0-1:
Boxes were left in twos and threes in the corners of rooms. Most have been gone through: a torn box you can see from the doorway, and it never has food. A sealed one is worth a long walk. Marked one I didn't get to.
— Dez
note-l0-2: Where the lights are dead the carpet's soaked, the air is cold, and some rooms are flooded. The cold keeps food and the water grows crops. But the dark pulls at the gear, and there are eyes in it. Bring a torch, not a candle.
note-l0-3:
Ruth, there's a room with a wooden floor, a door in each wall and a table under a chandelier. Nothing follows me in, and the gear turns forward while I'm there. I sit at the table and pretend it's ours. I've marked it.
— Tom
note-l0-4: Rooms papered red, lit red, walled off but for one narrow gap in each side. Nobody has touched the boxes in there, because nobody stays long enough; one had a key in it that hummed. In and out. Count to a hundred, then leave whatever you haven't got.
note-l0-5: A room full of square holes, two by two. Thirty steps down and you're in Level 2's tunnels, hot and dark, and there is no climbing back. It's the quickest way out of the Lobby I know. It only goes one way.
note-l0-6: The ceiling tiles come down, and what's on top of them sometimes doesn't: scrap wire, a bracket, rotten wood, once a stick of chalk. The slab above that never gives. Neither do the doors, nor the top of the wall where one level meets the next.
note-l0-7:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Bones on the carpet, a grey papery hive, crosses chalked on the walls round about: something lives there. At the heart of every den are two or three sealed boxes nobody dared take. In the Lobby they mostly watch. Mostly. The nearest is marked: keep out, or don't.
— Field Team 9 (six of us)
note-l0-8: The drywall breaks with any tool, quickest with an axe. Concrete wants a copper pickaxe and gives rubble; four rubble make a block to build with. Close off a corner, put a door in it, a light and a fire. When the lights go out, eyes come to the edge of the dark, even at home.
note-l0-9: A room hung with streamers, and a poster: TIME 4 FUN =). Don't touch it. If you do you won't be in the Lobby any more, and the people where you'll be are all smiling. A lit torch burns it.
note-l1-1:
The crates are the best food this side of the city: alone or stacked in the stalls, at the foot of the columns with the coloured cloths, in the camps. An emptied one, lid gone and straw in the corners, you can tell from across the aisle. Don't waste the walk.
— Dez
note-l1-2: The stair cores, black fire doors under lit EXIT signs, climb to another stairwell in Level 1, now and then in Level 4. You can walk back down. Where the level ends, the gaps in the wall are under EXIT signs too. Elsewhere the signs point at nothing.
note-l1-3:
People camp here, in the maintenance halls and round a burning barrel. They trade for rusty gears: salvage and hides for Almond Water, Firesalt, candles, bandages and seeds. Nothing comes near you while you're with one. They don't fight. Don't make them.
— Dez
note-l1-4:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Out towards the edge of Level 1 a whole section's lights go out at once: a Flickering. Hounds come with it and hunt until the lights return, a minute or two. Put a fire or a door between you and the dark. Look one in the eye and it stops and growls: a few seconds. Use them.
— Field Team 9 (six of us)
note-l1-5: The white halls behind the fire doors stay lit through a blackout. Workshops and toolboxes in there: a copper hammer, chisel, saw or knife now and then, and pry bars. A pry bar, two brackets and an iron nails and strips, opens a locked door for good in a few seconds if there's a room behind it. Everything near hears.
note-l1-6: People with no faces walk about here going nowhere. Wave to one (right-click it): it waves back and points the way out, as far as it knows. Hurt one and every one of them near turns on you.
note-l1-7: The car park holds you; the gear turns forward. The maintenance corridors don't, quite. Moths the size of your hand circle any open flame, and near the edges the females bite. A candle draws few, a closed lantern none, and smoke scatters them. Leave a settled one alone.
note-l1-8: A voice calling from out of sight, nearly human, coughing: a Skin-Stealer. Big, yellow, slow. Keep your distance, shut a door, keep a fire. Two red points under a shelf are rats with horns. They keep clear of a torch.
note-l1-9: Four doors that shouldn't be in Level 1. A red EXIT door in a solid car-park wall: it slams behind you, and then you run. A locked hall door under a glowing EXIT sign. Stairs into the ceiling with confetti on the steps. A grey door at the end of a maintenance hall, chalk arrows leading to it. I took the grey one.
note-l2-1:
Level 2 is hot: you will eat half again as fast. The three-wide mains run straight on for miles; the narrow ones between them mostly end. Stay on the mains. The whole level pulls at the gear: pass through, do not stay.
— A.L., survey
note-l2-2: Steel doors in the tunnel walls. Most are locked. Some open on a storeroom. A few that look exactly the same open on Level 3, 4 or 1, and you can walk back.
note-l2-3: The machine cabinets give copper. Oil drums sometimes still slosh with Almond Water. Toolboxes, trolleys, crates. Food is scarce: bring yours.
note-l2-4: An arm sticking up out of the floor, a finger twitching: a Clump. Walk round it if there's room. It hunts by ear: run or break things near it and it crawls after you. In a narrow tunnel, go back, or take the grab and be quick.
note-l2-5: One steel door in forty has a chalk circle on the wall beside it: that one goes to the Hub, and you can come back. And if a blind tunnel ends in a smooth new wall with red light at its foot, don't walk into it unless you can run for two minutes without stopping.
notetitle-l2-5: The circle and the red wall
note-l2-6:
Smilers like Level 2, and so do the rats, hairless in the heat. Near the edges the lights sometimes fail and something screams close by, and a pack of rats goes past at a run after it. Stand aside till the lights come back. Pell didn't.
— Dez
note-l3-1: Level 3 is hot brick and machinery: carry food. Tangles, squeezes you stoop through, wide galleries, transformer halls. White bars block the side ways you can see and can't reach. It pulls at the gear everywhere.
note-l3-2:
Clay lies under the manholes. Down the rungs into the flooded tunnels: freezing water, and the worst pull on the gear I have measured. Dig, and get out. The nearest manhole is marked.
— A.L., survey
note-l3-3: Coal is heaped by the generators, enough to smelt with. Turn it over: there are lumps of Firesalt in it. Copper wants a hotter fire than wood gives.
note-l3-4: A hushed hall of pale stone, a red carpet between the columns, candelabra, a winged statue at the end. A Sanctum. Nothing hostile goes in. There aren't many.
note-l3-5: Freight elevators in the electrical rooms go to other elevators in Levels 3, 4 and 5, and back. Everyone standing in the car rides along.
note-l3-6:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Scraping inside the walls means a Duller. It reaches through at whoever passes close: walk down the middle of the corridor. Drink Almond Water and it will not reach for you for five minutes. Face it and it runs. What it takes from your hands it drops wherever it went.
— Field Team 9 (five of us)
note-l3-7: Cable spools, stacked pipes (copper and lead), industrial fans: this is where copper comes from. The supply caches in the electrical rooms are worth the squeeze.
note-l4-1: Level 4 is quiet: cool, grey, almost empty. Desks break into planks, filing cabinets into paper. All of it holds you; the heart of it is the calmest ground there is before the city.
note-l4-2: Fountains, coolers, vending machines: Almond Water, a few bottles each. Break rooms have fridges with fruit and cheese. Some storerooms still hide a supply box.
note-l4-3: Stairwells and elevators stand together in building cores, with a restroom. The stairs mostly go to other stairs on this floor, now and then to the Lobby. The elevators go to 3, 4 or 5.
note-l4-4:
A few vending machines give nothing. Press the buttons and they take you to a food court, the same one every time: sealed, safe and full. Getting out is one way, and every door goes somewhere different.
— Dez
note-l4-5: A wooden doorframe standing on its own in an empty office. Walk through it and it's gone behind you, and you're in a library with no end. Most of its EXIT doors are locked. Bring food.
note-l4-6: Dullers here too: walk the middle of the corridor. A lantern is the light for this floor: the moths ignore it.
note-l5-1: The hotel goes on and the corridors wear on you. The Beverly Room doesn't: a ballroom with doors on every side and a game of Mahjong nobody finished. Nothing hostile goes in.
note-l5-2: Copper-cage elevators under a floor dial, rare, two wide: to other elevators in 3, 4 or 5, now and then Level 1. Most guest doors are locked for good. A few open, onto another part of the hotel, Level 3 or the Lobby, and you can walk back.
note-l5-3:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. An open door under a STAFF sign, stairs going up: the way into Level 6. Have your brightest light lit before you reach the top.
— Field Team 9 (four of us)
note-l5-4: STAFF ONLY doors open on the boiler halls: coal by the furnaces, Firesalt in the coal, and heat that will have you eating half again as fast. The worst pull on the gear in the hotel. Get the coal and go.
note-l5-5:
Ruth, there are children here with no faces. They come to look at me and run if I move too fast. When they all hurry away at once, the dogs are coming. They're not dogs.
— Tom
note-l5-6: Now and then one of the locked doors is cyan and says POOL. It opens: warm water, white tile, and you can walk back through the POOL door you come out beside.
note-l5-7: Wooden double doors with big letters: F-U-N. Behind them is a party that never stops. You can walk back out. They'll ask you to stay.
note-l6-1:
The corridors run on a grid. Every fourth is three wide and never breaks: find one and keep to it. The two-wide ones between are a maze with one way in. The narrow wet passages wind off a little way and stop.
— A.L., survey
note-l6-2:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Listen for waves: you hear them within a hundred and sixty paces of stairs down, louder as you close in, and chalk arrows on the corridor walls point there. The stairs come out in a room hung over the sea.
— Field Team 9 (four of us)
note-l6-3: A wire strung low across a straight corridor. Trip it and you're in a food court, bright and full. You can't get back to where you were, and nothing in there will hurt you.
note-l6-4: The ones who didn't make it left their packs at the dead ends: Almond Water, candles, rope, bandages, chalk, and often a note. Every dead end is worth one look.
note-l6-5: It's cold down here: wear something, or eat more. The scuttling and the whispering are mostly nothing. Scraping inside the wall is a Duller.
note-l6-6: There's a light switch on a wall now and then. It does nothing. I've tried every one I've found.
note-l61-1:
You're safe in here. The machines and fridges fill up again once a week. Eat.
— Dez
note-l61-2: Every door out shuts behind you. Rusty doors go to Level 6. Glass doors to Level 4 or 5. Vents to Level 3. Kitchen doors to another food court.
note-l61-3: One kind of kitchen door is different: the city's diners open into food courts, and you can walk back through the kitchen door you come out of.
note-l61-4:
Ruth, the gear turns forward faster here than anywhere. I sat a whole day. I almost stayed.
— Tom
note-l7-1: You come in from a room in the ceiling, over the drop. Shallows by the walls, then the twilight, then the midnight, then the abyss. Islands of black rock, some with a camp and a supply box.
note-l7-2: A ring of standing stones in the water. Dive in the middle and you come up in the Suburbs. One way.
note-l7-3: A cave mouth in the deep. Swim in and you come out on the 9th Road, in the caves. One way. Take a breath first.
note-l7-4: In the twilight zone, a patch of white tile on the seabed, faintly lit. Dive to it and you come up in warm water: the Poolrooms. One way.
note-l7-5:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Something vast circles out at the edge of sight. Stay below the twilight with your gear failing and it strikes, once, hard. In the abyss it may come at anyone. It cannot be fought. Surface.
— Field Team 9 (three of us)
note-l7-6: Driftwood is firewood. Fish bite. The seabed has wreck crates and lost packs. Mind the tar pools: they're scalding.
note-l8-1:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Stay on the 9th Road: gravel, lamps, our waypoints, camps along it. It forks and joins again, but follow the lamps and it runs on. Where the road meets another level it runs on through the wall.
— Field Team 9 (three of us)
note-l8-2:
Native copper and malachite. Cassiterite for tin, sphalerite for zinc, bismuth, gold in quartz, galena for lead, coal, and limonite, hematite and magnetite for iron. No silver ore: silver comes from the hotel. Loose ore lies on the cave floors.
— A.L., survey
note-l8-3: Almond Water seeps out of the rock beside the road. Hold a bottle to a seep and fill it; it comes back. Dullers won't reach for you near one.
note-l8-4: Drifters keep to the dark off the road; the lamps keep them off. The vents beside the road go to Level 2, and back.
note-l8-5: Halite grinds to salt in a quern; limestone and chalk grind to lime. There's a quern in Level 10's barns. Salt keeps meat, and salt with powdered sulfur makes Firesalt.
note-l8-6: It's cold: dress warm or eat more. The remains you find off the road were people who went to look at something.
note-l9-1:
Always midnight. The houses are the loot: kitchens and pantries for flour, salt and fat, garages for tools and seeds, dressers for clothes. Some are locked; that's what pry bars are for.
— Dez
note-l9-2:
Behind some houses a path runs through a field to a gate. Through it is Level 10, and you can walk back.
— Nell
note-l9-3: One house in a hundred and fifty is too cream and too clean: a doll's house. Its front door opens on Level 94, and you can walk back.
note-l9-4: One backyard pool in a few dozen is still full, lit teal. Dive to the bottom: the Poolrooms. One way.
note-l9-5: If the air goes cold all at once, a fog rolls in and voices start calling out of it, get indoors. There's only one of it, and it's far too big for any door. It goes in three minutes or so.
note-l9-6: Hares, foxes, raccoons, now and then a wolf. Hides make leather, and leather makes armour. The streets pull at the gear; don't stand about in them.
note-l10-1:
Safe, love, and steady. Ripe spelt, rye, flax and vegetables: cut them. The old furrows are spent: hoe fresh grass and plant there, within three steps of water. It never rains.
— Nell
note-l10-2:
Livestock in the paddocks, bee skeps by the farmhouses, cattails at the ponds for baskets, clay in the pond beds, a quern in the barns. Everything for a farm but somewhere to wake up.
— Nell
note-l10-3: A metre under the soil is a mass of worms. Dig into it and they come up biting, and the crops die round them. Don't dig down. And something waits half buried in the fields by the barns: watch for an arm.
note-l10-4:
In some barns a stretch of the east wall between the stalls isn't quite there: the boards a little out of true, dust hanging in front of them. Walk into it. Marked the one I found.
— Dez
note-l10-5: Dive to the bottom of a pond and you come up in the sea, Level 7. One way.
note-l11-1:
Nothing attacks in the city unless you start it. Groceries, pharmacies, hardware stores: food, bandages, copper tools, nails, rope. Almond Water in every machine and on every cart.
— Dez
note-l11-2: An apartment block's basement door goes to the Lobby. A parking garage ramp to Level 1, a subway maintenance door to 2, a substation door to 3, office tower elevators to 4, hotel elevators to 5. You can walk back through all of them.
note-l11-3: A dark doorway off an alley: Level 6. A rowhouse's front door: the Suburbs. A patch of wheat in a park: the fields. A diner's kitchen door: the food court, and back.
note-l11-4: An open manhole drops into Level 2, a street that has caved in into the caves, the deep middle of a park fountain into the sea. None of them come back.
note-l11-5: Public baths with a cyan door marked POOL: the Poolrooms. A cinema: walk up to the screen and on into the picture, and you fall out of the sky over green hills.
note-l11-6: A closed-down bookstore's door opens on a library with no end. Gym doors painted with a tiger, a parrot and a giraffe, at the back of a parking garage, open on a party. You can walk back out of both.
note-l11-7: A third of the buildings have no doors and black mirrors for windows. Nobody gets in. The floors above the shops are dark, and nobody has been up.
note-l37-1: Stand in lit water and it heals you, steadies you, and counts as rest. The dark corners pull at the gear. There's no food here at all: bring it.
note-l37-2: The stair pits go down further than you can see. Some passages are a swim under a wall. Know how long you can hold your breath before you find out.
note-l37-3:
POOL doors go out into the hotel, and back. A dry corridor whose tile turns to office carpet goes to Level 4. One whose tile turns to concrete and asphalt goes to the Hub. A tunnel of arches ends in a black round mouth over the sea. If a corridor is lit red, turn round.
— A.L., survey
note-l37-4: Crusts of Epsom salt dry on the rims in the dark corners. Two of them over a linen make a poultice as good as any.
note-l37-5: Far out the water turns thick and red, and there's chanting. Red Water heals everything. It also takes away, for good, how steady you can ever be again.
note-l37-6: The pit nobody has found the bottom of comes up in a backyard pool in the Suburbs. One way.
note-l94-1: Everything here moves a frame at a time. By day it's safe. When the siren tune slows and goes flat, get indoors: the Animations come out at night, and they never come inside.
note-l94-2: If they find you outside, stand still. Quite still, a few seconds, and they take you for a doll. The paper ones fall apart in water.
note-l94-3:
Iceboxes in every house: cheese, butter, beans. Milk vans by the plazas with Almond Milk, filled again each week. Fountains and water towers for Almond Water.
— Dez
note-l94-4:
Dig the turf for soil, love. Under it is red modelling clay, and blue clay a little further down. All the pottery you want.
— Nell
note-l94-5: A rusted gate with no sign on a hilltop, at dusk and dawn only: Level 10. One house in forty opens back onto the Suburbs. Don't open the door of a house that's full of water unless you want the sea.
note-l94-6: Towards the middle the houses come apart into heaps of furniture. Follow the strangeness to a glass mountain and a castle. Touch nothing in it: tin soldiers wind up and come for a minute and a half.
note-l94-7: The King sits in stone at a long table. Sit in the second chair and he makes your nightmare out of clay. It's only as strong as you think it is: drink your Almond Water first. Win, and he carries you out.
note-run-1: The door's locked behind you and there's no other way back. When the chained door bursts, run, and don't stop. Toys, boxes, cords and fallen ceiling on the floor will trip you if you sprint over them: jump them.
note-run-2: Don't take the door if the hall turns beside it. The real one is at a dead end, light under it. The EXIT doors at the bends have a dead letter in the sign and open on an empty room. Don't stop. They're still there.
note-run-3: Eat the energy bars on the bedside table before the door goes: half a minute quicker. Some halls have a Safe Zone, a room they won't come into. They wait outside. After a couple of hours they stop waiting.
note-run-4: In the dark last stretch, cracked floor means a hole just past it. It drops you into the caves, if you'd rather that than what's behind you.
note-run-5:
Out the far end you're in Level 1, the office or a library with no end, always the same for the same hall. Runners who didn't make it lie along the way; one had a key that hummed. And once you're out, it won't let you in again.
— Dez
note-fun-1: Everyone here is smiling, and they're not people. They bite, and a bite turns into a fever that only goes down once you're out of here. Bandage or poultice a bite within half a minute and it doesn't take. If the fever fills, you don't leave.
note-fun-2: Wear a party hat and hold a red balloon, and from more than three steps off they take you for one of them, as long as you don't run or hit anything. They're slow and short-sighted: keep your distance. The hats come off the dead ones; the balloons off the little ones.
note-fun-3:
One gift in five is a popper, and everything near hears it. Birthday cake and cookies are fine. Don't eat the red velvet.
— Dez
note-fun-4: A balloon tied to nothing, in the dark corridors: it stings and holds you. Don't pop it close. The gas comes out.
note-fun-5: The service stairs go down to Level 1, the FUN doors to the hotel, a waiting room's white door to the city, and you can come back by each. A poster back to front in a room where the party's over goes to the office. Over the side of the deck is the sea. The bottom of the deep ball pit is somewhere else entirely.
note-fun-lie: Level Fun is completely safe =) There is a party in the room I marked. Come join us!
note-end-1:
Two EXIT doors in three never open. The ones that do always go to the same place: mostly Level 1, sometimes the Hub, the city, the office or the hotel, and you can come back. Write down which open. The cards in the catalogue drawers point at one that does.
— A.L., survey
note-end-2: Every so often the lights stutter, the floor shakes, and for a few seconds it's somewhere else: the Lobby, the office, a street at night, warm water, green hills, snow. Walk into a wall while it lasts and you go there. Not the snow.
note-end-3: Stay a couple of hours and the gear starts slipping. The central hall holds you. Shelves that lean come down at a touch, loudly, and when the lights go out there's something grinning in the dark.
note-end-4: The computers buzz until you turn one on. It shows the doors that open near it, once, and dies. One in four says =) instead. Don't.
note-end-5: Some departments are somebody's office, a hotel corridor, a house, the Lobby, made of shelves. Each has one real door, to the place it copies. Some stockrooms have a ladder up to a vent that lets you out over green hills. Service desks and catalogues sometimes hold a key that hums.
note-hub-1:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Nothing hunts here and the gear turns forward, but it is cold and there is nothing to eat. Bring food.
— Field Team 9 (two of us)
note-hub-2: Every carved door wants its own level's key, turned three times, and the key is gone after. Three open for anyone: Level 1 in tunnel 7, the city in tunnel 10, and 178, the food court, in tunnel 5. None of them let you back. Hold a key here and listen: it chimes from the way its door is.
note-hub-3: The keys are found in their own levels, mostly in the worst places: the Lobby's Red Rooms, the flooded tunnels and Sanctums of Level 3, the red water of the Poolrooms, the King's castle. Sometimes in a den, now and then a sealed box. In the long red hall, on the runners who didn't make it.
note-hub-4: In the Tower a man gives you one key, of a level you have been to. Right-click him to see which; sneak and right-click to take it. He walks you to its door. He never lets you in again, and if you break anything in there he throws you out with nothing.
note-hub-5:
By the city door the M.E.G. keep a doorstep carpet: their man sells two keys a week for rusty gears, and their register shows where the open doors are. The pink door with the ribbon opens for anyone carrying something cute. A hole in the road drops you out of the sky over green hills. Where a wall's seams don't meet, walk through: the office.
— Dez
note-l974-1: It's watching. It won't hurt you. Don't break its things and don't strike it: it puts the lights out and empties the larder.
note-l974-2: It wants the cute thing you brought. Sneak and right-click with it in your hand and it comes for it. Give it over, sleep, and you wake somewhere quiet, always the same somewhere from the same house.
note-l974-3:
Ruth, after most of a day the pink starts to press, and the food turns to sugar. If you've lost what you brought, wait a day: it'll take anything cute and send you home.
— Tom
note-r-l0-1: The Red Rooms keep keys. About one box in a dozen in there has a Level Key that hums when you strike it. I marked the nearest red block. Don't stay past a hundred.
note-r-l0-2:
Ruth, I moved home to the Manila Room. The gear turns forward there, nothing follows me in, and four doors means four ways out. I've marked it for whoever comes after. Use a temporal gear on the floor there.
— Tom
note-r-l1-1:
M.E.G. BRIEFING, RESTRICTED. Level 1 has two doors worth knowing. A locked hall door off the maintenance halls under a glowing EXIT sign, about one in twenty-five: The End, and back. A grey door with a carved ring of marks at the end of a hall, chalk arrows leading to it: the Hub, and back. Nearest marked.
— Field Team 9
note-r-l3-1:
Fair copy, Level 3. In the flooded tunnels under the floor, about one box in a dozen holds a Level Key. The Sanctums keep them too. Clay underfoot all the way. Nearest manhole marked.
— A.L.
note-r-l4-1: The vending machines that take you are always the same ones, and each always takes you to the same food court. If you find one, mark it: it's the only door into that place you'll ever get to choose.
note-r-l5-1: One locked guest door in a hundred and fifty is F-U-N. Some are cyan POOL doors. Most guest doors that open lead on into the hotel, but some go to Level 3 or the Lobby, and the Lobby ones are the best road home there is. Nearest safe room marked.
note-r-l6-1:
M.E.G. BRIEFING, RESTRICTED. Level 6 trip wires run low across straight corridors only. The stairs down are in chambers deep in the level; the waves carry a hundred and sixty paces. Nearest way down marked.
— Field Team 9
note-r-l7-1:
Fair copy, Level 7. The island camps keep a supply box each, and the wreck crates on the seabed have never been opened. The white tile lies in the twilight zone, not deeper. Nearest untouched box marked.
— A.L.
note-r-l8-1:
Fair copy, Level 8: native copper and malachite (green); cassiterite, tin; sphalerite, zinc; bismuthinite; gold in quartz; galena, lead; limonite, hematite and magnetite, iron. No silver ore at all: take silver from the hotel's silverware, or from galena deep down. Halite and limestone for the quern.
— A.L.
note-r-l9-1: The doll's house is one in a hundred and fifty: cream, too clean, no wear on the step. Its door goes to Motion and back. The full pool is one backyard in a few dozen, lit teal at midnight: the Poolrooms, one way.
note-r-l10-1:
Love, the barn wall: the east side, between the stalls, boards out of true, in a little under half the barns. I've marked the nearest one I know. My lad went through to the city and came back with tinned peaches.
— Nell
note-r-l11-1:
City secrets: the diner kitchen doors go to the food court and walk back, the only door into the Snackrooms that does. The cinema screen drops you over Motion. The bookstore is the way into The End that lets you back out.
— Dez
note-r-l37-1:
Fair copy, the dry corridors: about one in five turns to asphalt (the Hub, and back); about one in seven is lit red and ends in an EXIT door (Level !, no way back); the rest turn to office carpet (Level 4). Read the floor before you walk on.
— A.L.
note-r-l94-1: One of the throne room's four doors opens, a different one each day. With your gear full the King's clay thing hits at a quarter of its strength; with it empty, twice as hard. The first time you win he gives you a shard of his crown, and the Animations take whoever carries it for one of their own.
note-r-end-1:
Fair copy, The End. One EXIT door in three opens, always to the same place. Of those: four in ten to Level 1, one in four to the Hub, three in twenty to the city's bookstore, one in ten each to the office and the hotel. The fake rooms: an office goes to Level 4, a hotel to 5, a house to 9, the Lobby to 0; the snow goes nowhere. Nearest working door marked.
— A.L.
note-r-hub-1:
M.E.G. BRIEFING, RESTRICTED. A Level Key held in the Hub chimes from its door's direction, and rings out within eight paces of it. The keys for Level 1, the city and 178 are wasted: those doors open for anyone.
— Field Team 9
note-r-run-1: What I worked out the third time. Seventeen halls. The real exit is at a dead end with no turn either side. One hall in three has a hole near the end, cracked floor before it, down to the caves. One in five has a Safe Zone: they wait outside for three hours, then they come in. Real exit marked.
note-r-fun-1: A party hat on your head and a red balloon in your hand, and from more than three steps they take you for one of them, so long as you don't run or hit. Bandage a bite inside half a minute or the fever takes. The fever only goes down outside, slowly, and Almond Water helps. The way out I used is marked.
note-ra01:
M.E.G. BRIEFING, RESTRICTED. Hub entrances, verified. Level 1: in the outer half of the maintenance halls, a grey door with a carved sigil over it in the middle of a hall block's north wall; chalk arrows along the corridor point to it. Level 2: one locked steel door in forty, a chalk circle on the wall beside it. Level 37: a dry corridor whose tile turns to concrete and asphalt. All three walk back.
— Field Team 9
note-ra02:
Fair copy. The food courts (Level 6.1) can be entered four ways: a hungry vending machine in Level 4 (the same few always take you); a wire strung low across a straight corridor in Level 6; a diner's kitchen door in the city, which walks back; and the open carved door marked 178 in the Hub's fifth tunnel. I know of no other.
— A.L.
note-ra03: If you carry something cute (a plush, a flower, a seashell) through any doorway that goes somewhere, one time in twenty you end up in a pink house that's yours, with something very tall in it. One in six if it's in your hand. It never hurts you. Give it the thing you brought and you wake somewhere quiet. Not twice in two days.
note-ra04:
M.E.G. BRIEFING. Our man on the doorstep carpet by the Hub's city door sells two Level Keys a week, thirty to forty-five rusty gears each, only for levels somebody has been to. The Keymaster in the Tower gives one free, of a level you have been to, once: right-click to see which, sneak and right-click to take. Break nothing in the Tower.
— Field Team 9
note-ra05: Locks. A pry bar gives on a locked door in about four seconds, for good, but only if there's a room behind it. A door set in solid wall won't give. A door that goes somewhere was never locked: just open it. Twenty-four uses. Everything near hears it.
note-ra06:
Ruth, a man showed me: a temporal gear in my left hand, a knife in my right, and hold right-click. The gear's steadiness goes into me, at the cost of the gear and some blood. About one supply box in a hundred has a gear. Keep one for home and one for this.
— Tom
note-ra07:
M.E.G. BRIEFING, RESTRICTED. Far from home, now and then, a grey door appears behind you where there was wall. It goes to the Hub, one way, and it is gone in five minutes. If you want the Hub, turn round more often.
— Field Team 9 (one of us)
note-ra08:
Fair copy, ways to the Poolrooms: a cyan POOL door in the hotel, or the city's public baths (both walk back); a patch of white tile on Level 7's seabed in the twilight zone, faintly lit; the one backyard pool in a few dozen in the Suburbs that is still full, lit teal. The last two are one way.
— A.L.
note-ra09:
Fair copy, Level 10 to the city. Not every barn: a little under half. The east wall, between the stalls, where the boards look out of true and dust hangs in front of them. Walk into it. The thin spot you leave on the far side stays.
— A.L.
note-ra10:
Stash list, for whoever. Sealed, untouched. I counted it twice and didn't take it, because I couldn't carry it. Marked it for you. Food's food.
— Dez
note-ra11: Ways into Motion: a doll's house in the Suburbs (one in a hundred and fifty, walks back); a cinema screen in the city; a ladder to a vent in some of The End's stockrooms; a hole in the road in the Hub's far tunnels; the deep ball pit in Level Fun, into the castle. Be indoors by dusk.
note-ra12:
Fair copy, the last. I have walked every door I could find and written each one down. They are honest: every one leads where it led before. None of them leads out. I am going to the Manila Room to sit at the table for a while.
— A.L.
note-s01: Day 40. Counted the ceiling tiles in one room: 117. Came back through it today. 118.
note-s02: If anyone finds Marcy, tell her I went left.
note-s03: The hum is a B flat. I had perfect pitch, before.
note-s04: Found a room with my handwriting on the wall. I don't remember writing it. It says don't trust the room.
note-s05: Three of us. Then two. Dana went to look at the light that was on in the far room. The light's still on.
note-s07:
Ate the last crackers. They were good crackers.
— Dez
note-s08: Somebody has been moving my chalk arrows. Or I drew them wrong. Either way, I'm going right.
note-s09:
Things I know: water is real. The gear is real. The doors are honest. Nothing else is.
— A.L.
note-s10:
If you're keeping these, you're keeping more than I did. Good.
— Nell
journal-empty: Nothing yet. Notes you read are kept here.
note-pocket-given: There is a folded note in your pocket. You don't remember putting it there.
waypoint-note-hubdoor: A way into the Hub (a note)
waypoint-note-hubopen: A carved door that opens (a note)
waypoint-note-staffdoor: STAFF ONLY: one in six opens (a note)
itemdesc-wanderernote-folded: Folded small and kept dry, written in ink. Whoever wrote it meant it to last. Right-click to read it.
blockdesc-loosenote-door: Someone left a note here. Right-click to pick it up.
blockdesc-loosenote-way: Someone left a note here. Right-click to pick it up.
blockdesc-loosenote-cache: Someone left a note here. Right-click to pick it up.
blockdesc-loosenote-refuge: Someone left a note here. Right-click to pick it up.
blockdesc-loosenote-folded: Someone left a note here. Right-click to pick it up.
note-l10-6:
Out past the farmsteads, love, some of the windmills have a red light on the cap, five in a line. Follow them. At the end there's a building that has no business being there, PARADISE in pink letters and music behind dark glass. Its revolving door goes somewhere warm, and you can walk back. Throw the lever by a windmill's door and its light turns green, so you know where you've been.
— Nell
note-l3999-1: Nothing hunts where the neon is lit. It's warm, the gear turns forward, faster in the lobbies, and the violet pools mend you while you stand in them. The faceless staff behind the counters can't be hurt and won't hurt you; ask one and it points the way to a lobby. Right-click a mall directory and it gives the way to the nearest food court and lobby. More wanderers camp here than anywhere.
note-l3999-2:
Every machine pays you once a day. Hold right-click and play it out. The little cabinets pay up to three tickets, pinball up to four, the racers, dance pads and skee-ball one to five, and now and then one hits a jackpot of twelve. The claw pays nothing, but one go in four it drops you a plush. Forty tickets a day is all the machines will give you, all of them together.
— Dez
note-l3999-3:
Tickets in your hand at a prize counter, and you get a prize from the dearest tier you can pay. 5: candy, a soda, a candle, a glow bracelet, a plush. 15: seeds, bandages, firesalt, neon tubing, a neon lamp. 40: a lantern, a backpack, a pry bar, six Almond Water. 200: a temporal gear. The food stalls sell a hot tray for 6.
— Dez
note-l3999-4:
The vending machines take a bottle of Almond Water and give you a snack or a can: chips, a candy bar, popcorn, cotton candy, soda, cashew water, Paradise Pop. They never run empty. Popcorn's grain, love; most of the rest is sugar and fizz. The trays from the stalls fill you best.
— Nell
note-l3999-5:
Finding: the dead machines break down. Circuit boards melt to copper in a crucible, ten to an ingot; coin mechanisms to brass, five to an ingot. Plastic burns. Dead neon gives tubing. Two tubing, two plastic, a circuit board and a glow bracelet make two neon lamps of the bracelet's colour; plastic and tubing make two lilac bracelets. The machines that still work cannot be broken.
— A.L., survey
note-l3999-6:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. Toward the far edge, some blocks of the mall have gone dark: Level 3999.1. The neon flickers and fails for a stretch before it. Inside it is cold and the gear runs down fast. Smilers in the dark, Hound packs, Partygoers. The prize cases and ticket piles in there belong to whoever carries them out. A rusted machine in a row of cabinets is no machine: walk into it and you are in the dark.
— Field Team 9
note-l3999-7: A lobby's revolving door walks you out into a car park in the wheat fields, and back. One STAFF ONLY door in six opens on the Hub, and back; the rest are locked. Some game rooms have a little arcade at the back with an elevator down to the Lobby, and back. Play a cabinet with another place on its marquee to the end and it takes you there, one way. A drain at the bottom of a violet pool drops you into the Poolrooms.
note-l188-1: The window you climbed in by shows where you came from, and climbing back through it takes you there. The other ground-floor windows that show somewhere else lead there too. The rest are rooms: blinds down, lit, dark, changing every day or so. Look before you go in anywhere.
note-l188-2:
Ruth, never open a blind from inside a room. A man did, in front of me, and he was gone, and the window lit up with a hallway I'd never seen. The door shut and wouldn't open for three days. Each window always goes to the same place, so you can tell where he went by looking. I hope it has weather.
— Tom
note-l188-3: Someone standing in a lit window, waving: count which room it is and stay out of it. Within six steps you hear whispering. Within two, an arm comes out of the glass and pulls. Hit it twice, or get three or four steps clear, before it has you at the glass: six seconds there and you go through, and nobody comes back from that. They move to other windows every night. The shapes at the edge of your eye are nothing. Don't look.
note-l188-4:
The rooms are warm, love, and the courtyard isn't. Shut a room's door behind you and nothing comes in, unless someone was waving in its window. Wardrobes have clothes and cloth, minibars Almond Water, juice and crackers, and beds give cloth. Breakfast in the lobby: cereal and juice from the machines. The housekeeping carts sometimes hold a keycard; it opens the locked rooms, never the ones held shut.
— Nell
note-l188-5:
M.E.G. FIELD NOTICE. The Hub has one window, in a tunnel wall: climb through and you come down in the courtyard beside the window that leads back. Level Fun has one, a party room's window with confetti on the sill. The Lobby and Level 1 have windows where no window should be. All of them walk back.
— Field Team 9
note-l188-6:
Finding: one fire door on each upper floor, EXIT over it, push bar. Second floor: Level 1. Third: the hotel. Fourth: the office. Fifth: the pipes. Each walks back. The lifts are out of order and the front door in the lobby is locked; the stairs are in the north-west corner.
— A.L., survey
note-l188-7:
Iron ring in the middle of the deck. Lift the hatch and drop: a long way down through the black, into warm water. The Poolrooms. No way back up.
— Dez
note-r-l3999-1:
Fair copy, ways into 3999. Level 10: five windmills in a line, red lights on their caps, lead to a lone arcade; its revolving door walks in, and back. The city: a stretch of alley wall flickering purple, one block in three hundred; walk into it, and back. The far Poolrooms: glowing magenta tiles at the bottom of the deepest water; dive, one way. The End: about one computer in twenty runs a program nobody started. The Hub: the door marked 3999.
— A.L.
note-r-l3999-2:
Ticket sense. Hold only what you mean to spend: the counter takes the dearest tier your hand can pay, so walk up with two hundred and you get the gear whether you wanted it or not. Forty a day means five days of machines for a gear. Or go into the dark: the ticket piles there are a handful each, the prize cases are free, and nothing counts what you take.
— Dez
note-r-l188-1:
Fair copy, Level 188. Twelve ground-floor windows show other places and lead there, and back: the Lobby (three), Level 1 (two), the pipes, the office, the hotel, the dark, the Suburbs, the Hub, the party. A blind opened from inside any other room goes somewhere fixed: most often the Lobby, then Level 1, the office or the hotel; one in fifty to The End. A window lit with somewhere is a sealed room.
— A.L.
note-r-l188-2:
M.E.G. BRIEFING, RESTRICTED. Ways into 188: a window where no window should be, in about one cell in three hundred of the outer Lobby, or one car park in two hundred and fifty in Level 1; the Hub's tunnel window; Level Fun's confetti window. All four walk back. Out without a window: the fire doors upstairs, or the hatch, one way.
— Field Team 9
guide-food-title: Game Mechanic: Food, Heat and Cold
guide-food-text:
Food, Heat and Cold
There is no winter here. There is also no harvest.

Hunger
You go hungry a quarter faster than in an ordinary world, and above 30 °C faster still: about 6% more for every degree, up to half again as fast. Level 2 (38 °C) and the boiler halls of Levels 3 and 5 (42 °C) are the worst; Level 3 (35 °C) and Level 3999's natatoria (34 °C) are hot too. Level 1 (28 °C) is warm but costs nothing extra. Moving burns food; sprinting burns more; standing still burns almost nothing. There is no thirst: Almond Water is food, not drink.

Cold
Nothing here is cold enough to kill you quickly, but the cold levels are cold enough to hurt without clothes: Level 6 (8 °C), Level 8 (9 °C), Level 7 (12 °C, 6 °C under the sea), the Hub's tunnels (6 °C, and 2 °C in the Far Tunnels), Level 188's courtyard (8 °C), Level 3999's Blackout (14 °C) and the open decks of Level Fun (11 °C). Clothes come from Level 5's wardrobes and suitcases, Level 9's dressers and Level 188's rooms; Level 5's furnaces and boilers and Level 1's burn barrels give off warmth. Level 0's blackout zones (10 °C) are the useful cold: food in a chest there keeps more than twice as long as in the Lobby proper, and any fully enclosed room counts as a cellar for the vanilla preservation rules.

What there is to eat
Only sealed boxes and crates hold food; most were found torn or prised open long ago. Rooms behind locked doors were never picked over (see the pry bar in Finding the Way), and neither were the hearts of dens.
- Almond Water: fills a little, heals 1, restores 15% stability. Supply boxes, supply crates, drums; fountains, coolers and vending machines (Level 4, the city); seeps in the rock beside Level 8's road; the hand pumps on Level 10's farms; vendors' carts (the city); the towns' fountains and the hilltop water towers of Level 94.
- Crackers, canned beans: supply boxes, crates, cardboard boxes, fridges, pantries.
- Fruit and cheese: fridges (Levels 4, 9, the city). Flour, salt, fat: kitchen cupboards and pantries (Level 9, city groceries).
- Chips, chocolate, soda, Cashew Water (8% stability): the Snackrooms; city stores.
- Fish: Level 7, and seaweed in its shallows. Game and berries: Level 9. Crops, livestock, honey, berries: Level 10, where the fields stand ripe. Mushrooms: the bracket fungi of Level 8's caves, some of them.
- Level 94: iceboxes in every house (cheese, butter, beans), Almond Milk (10% stability) in the milk vans by the towns' plazas, Almond Water from the fountains and water towers.
- Level 37 has no food at all. Take enough with you. Its dark corners hold Epsom salt for poultices, and the Sanguine Reservoir's red sprouts give Red Water, which heals every wound and lowers for good how steady you can ever be.
- Energy Bars: only in Level !: the bedside table, trays beside doors, the Safe Zone's shelves. Eating one gives you a second wind: a little more speed for half a minute.
- Level Fun: birthday cake (rightmouse a cake for a slice), cookies from the plates, Almond Water on some tables, pumpkins in the Halloween rooms, onions from popped balloons. Red Velvet =): do not eat. It fills you well, but costs you stability and the party gets into you (Party Fever). Gifts hold what wanderers left; one in five is a popper, and the bang carries.
- The End has no food: Almond Water from the coolers in the stockrooms, nothing else. Memory Juice restores 20% stability, and for a while everything feels like home. The Junkies want it.
- Kitty's House (Level 974): the fridge and the pantry give one thing per rightmouse, six at most, one more every 2 hours: bread, cheese, fruit, strawberry milk. After a day half of it is sweets (marshmallows, candy), after two days all of it. Now and then a remembered meal lies on the table, the best food in the house. Every tap fills a bucket, jug or bowl with water.
- The Hub has nothing to eat. Bring food and clothes.
- Level 3999: tray meals at the food stalls, 6 tickets each (burgers, pizza, noodles, tacos, ice cream, pretzels: filling, and they heal a little). The vending machines take one Almond Water for chips, a candy bar, popcorn, cotton candy, soda, cashew water or Paradise Pop, and never run out. See the tickets in Salvage.
- Level 188: the lobby's breakfast dispensers (rightmouse): cereal and juice boxes, three of each, then empty; the minibars in the rooms.

Food that comes back
See Home and Expeditions: fish, game, crops, livestock, the refilling dispensers, and a farm of your own. Everything else is finite: a level is a larder that empties.

World settings
When a world is created, Backrooms scarcity (under Survival challenges) sets how much food and drink the Backrooms leave you: Plentiful doubles it, Sparse leaves six parts in ten, Scarce about a third. It scales everything you can eat or drink, Almond Water among it, in every box, crate, cupboard and fridge; how much the vending machines, water coolers, fountains and Kitty's fridge and pantry hold, and how soon they refill (on Scarce, what refills does so after three weeks rather than one, and about one in three of Level 4's vending machines and water coolers is empty from the start); and how much livestock grazes in Level 10. In new worlds on Sparse or Scarce, Level 9's gardens and Level 10's crops, vegetable patches and berry bushes bear less too (by the scarcity the world was created with, even if it is changed later). Seeds, notes and tools are not affected. Backrooms map sets how much the map helps (see Finding the Way).
guide-farlevels-text:
The Levels Beyond the Rings
No wall leads here. You get in by the ways in Ways Between Levels, and by no other.

Level 37, Sublimity (the Poolrooms). White tile and warm, still water, rooms and pools that make no sense, light falling through slits from somewhere you never see, and corners left in the dark. Nothing lives here; no one has ever met anyone. Standing in lit water heals you, steadies you and counts as rest, so it is the place to recover between expeditions. But there is no food at all, the dark corners drain you, and the deep water is where people drown: stair pits go down further than you can see, and some passages are a swim under a wall. Crusts of Epsom salt dry on the rims in the dark.

Level 37.1, the Sanguine Reservoir. Far out in the Poolrooms, the light thins, the water turns thick and slow and red, and red sprouts on the pool floors are all the light there is. A distant chanting draws people in, louder the nearer you come. Stability drains fast. What the drowned left lies on the bottom, untouched; and the red water heals everything, at a price.

Level 94, Motion. You fall into it out of the sky, and land softly. A stop-motion picture of the 1950s: round green hills, a two-storey cream house on each, winding roads behind white picket fences, small towns round fountains of Almond Water, siren poles playing the same tune all day. Food in plenty, and the ground is clay: dig the turf for soil, the red modelling clay under it for clay (blue clay a little way down), and three to seven blocks down, over much of the hills, pale seams of fire clay, the only fire clay in the Backrooms and the key to iron and steel. By night the Animations come out, and hunt anything that does not look animated: be indoors by dusk (when the tune slows and goes flat, from half past five, it is nearly time; they are out from eight until half past five in the morning), or stand quite still and be taken for a doll. Towards the middle the houses come apart, room by room, into heaps of furniture; follow the strangeness (or the white castle on the horizon, which glows a little after dusk) and you reach the glass mountain and the King's castle, which drains you.

Level !, Run For Your Life! You are taken there, and the door slams behind you. A hospital room in red light, an alarm, something hammering at a chained door (it holds for twelve seconds, or four once you are in the hall). Take what is in the bedside table and the cabinet (Almond Water, Energy Bars, a bandage) and go: the way out is the door under the lit EXIT sign, and it sticks (pull it three times). Then run, and don't stop: about a minute and a quarter at a sprint, some 480 blocks of hall lit only by EXIT signs (600 in worlds made before 0.514.0). Swerve round beds and chairs, jump fallen shelving, mind the doors that fly open and the signs that burst into flame, and jump the junk on the floor (toys, boxes, tangled cords, fallen ceiling): sprint over it on the ground and you trip. The horde behind you runs at four fifths of your sprint, a little slower just after it bursts out: it falls back while you run and catches you the moment you stop, and being caught is death. Telling the exits apart: a false exit has a turn in the hall beside it, its EXIT sign is darker with the X burnt out, and the gap under its door is dark. The real exit is at a dead end with no turn either side, under a bright EXIT sign, with a faint light in the gap under the door; it leads to Level 1, Level 4 or The End. Escape once and the Backrooms never send you there again. A blue stretch of hall is the Safe Zone: nothing comes in, not into the hall nor its side rooms, so rest and eat, but go when the walls shudder (after about two hours; at three the horde comes in).

Level Fun =). Endless party rooms on a ship that cannot be this big: balloons, streamers, cake on every table, a tinny "Happy Birthday" somewhere through the walls. A room with a balloon arch over its door and music playing has guests: tall yellow Partygoers with a smile carved into the face (see What Lives Here). Their tables are the best larder in the Backrooms. Dark service corridors hold balloons tied to nothing: don't touch them. Anything marked =) is a lie, wanderers' notes included. It drains you everywhere, and the open decks are cold (11 °C). You arrive in an elevator lobby; the ways home are rare: stairs into the ceiling (Level 1), wooden doors marked FUN (the hotel), a waiting room's door (the city).

The End. A library that goes on forever, and the cruellest trap in the Backrooms: it looks like the way out. Empty maple shelving under fluorescent lights, and in the middle a curved desk under bronze letters: THE END.
- Doors marked EXIT stand in the stockrooms and at the corners of the central hall. Two in three never open. The rest always lead to the same place: Level 1, the Hub, the city, the Office or the Hotel, and back again.
- Fake realities: out in the library, places you know (the Lobby, an office, a hotel corridor, a house, a snowfield) that the shelves blend into. Some have a real door in their middle.
- A vent at the top of a ladder in some stockrooms drops you into Level 94.
- The computers buzz until you turn one on. It shows the name of the place and dies for good, but marks on your map the nearest ways out that open. If a screen says =), you are not staying; now and then one runs TRUEEND.EXE instead, and takes you to Level 3999.
- The longer you stay, the less sure of yourself you are: after two in-game hours inside, stability drains a little more each minute. It is kindest in the middle; outward it drains, and the collapses and fake realities drain badly.
- Distortions: now and then the floor shakes and for a few seconds you are somewhere else. Walk into a wall or a shelf then, and you will be (the snowfield leads nowhere). And the lights go out for a minute or two: carry a light.
- No food (see Food, Heat and Cold), but furniture, ladders and books for a home. In the Home fake realities live the Junkies, who trade only with someone carrying Memory Juice.

The Hub. A hidden crossroads of road tunnels under orange lamps, silent and cold (14 °C at the centre, 6 °C in the tunnels, 2 °C far out). Ten numbered tunnels run out from a tower at its centre, and both walls are lined with great concrete doors, a crop circle carved over each. Every door leads to a level, and almost all are locked.
- Safe: nothing hostile follows you in, it restores you, and resting here counts. But there is nothing to eat: bring food and clothes.
- Open doors: three are always open, each one way: Level 1 in Tunnel 7, Level 11 in Tunnel 10, the Snackrooms ("178") in Tunnel 5. The M.E.G. marked them, and their outpost by the Level 11 door has a register (rightmouse) that marks them on your map, and a wanderer who sells Level Keys. A second camp keeps the Level 1 door.
- Level Keys: any other door needs its level's key (see Salvage). Hold a key in your hand in the Hub and listen: it rings from the way its door lies, and close by the door goes on your map. Use the door with the key: three turns, the key is gone, and there is no way back through.
- The pink door with a ribbon bow needs no key, only something cute on you: it leads to Kitty's House.
- A lit window in a tunnel wall, a room behind it: climb through (walk into it, or rightmouse) to Level 188's courtyard, and back.
- The way back is the plain grey door you came in by.
- The Far Tunnels: past the third ring road the lamps die out and the place stops restoring you. Out there are a wall that isn't there (Level 4), holes in the road (Level 94), and tunnels where the concrete turns to white tile (Level 37).
- The Tower: ten ornate doors at the inner ends of the tunnels. You are let in once. Its keeper wants you gone, and will give you one key to make sure of it. Break nothing inside, and mind the balcony: fall from it and you are thrown out into the tunnels.

Level 974, Kitty's House. Not a place you can walk to. Cross into any level with something cute on you (a plush, a flower, a seashell) and, once in a while, you are taken here instead, more often if you hold it in your hand. A small pink house with no way outside: its windows are paintings. Nothing hostile comes: lights, water from every tap, a bed you can sleep in, a fridge and a pantry that fill again, and an old computer whose e-mail explains the rest. Kitty lives here: very tall, faceless, black as cloth, and it will never hurt you. It watches.
- Be a good guest. Break anything in the house, or strike Kitty, and the lights go out, the food is gone, your stability takes a blow, and Kitty will not see you for a day.
- Don't stay long. After 18 hours the pink starts to wear on you (and more so at 36 and 60); after a day half the food is sweets, after two days all of it.
- To leave, hold the cute thing you brought (not what you found here), sneak and rightmouse to call ("Here Kitty, Kitty, Kitty!"), then rightmouse Kitty when it holds out its arm. You fall asleep and wake somewhere safe (Level 4, 37 or the Snackrooms), the same place every time for your house, and for three minutes nothing comes near. Lost what you brought? After a day Kitty takes anything cute, but you wake in Level 0.
- The house is yours: what you leave in it is there next time.

Level 3999, the Neon Paradise. An arcade the size of a city: carpet that glows under black light, neon on every wall, music from nowhere. Concourses eighteen blocks high with galleries along both sides and moving walkways that carry you; game rooms and halls, food courts, bowling lanes, lobbies with a revolving door, pools of warm violet water. Warm (24 °C; the pools 34 °C) and safe: nothing hostile comes where the neon is lit, and the gear turns forward, most in the lobbies. Standing in a pool heals you slowly. Faceless Arcade Attendants keep the counters; a mall directory (rightmouse) marks the nearest food court and lobby on your map. More wanderers camp here than anywhere (one lobby in four).
- Machines: hold rightmouse on one to play it out. Each pays you tickets once a day (little cabinets 0 to 3, pinball 0 to 4, racers, dance pads and skee-ball 1 to 5, now and then a jackpot of 12; the claw drops a plush one go in four, nothing otherwise), and no more than 40 tickets a day from all of them together.
- Prize counters take the dearest tier the tickets in your hand can pay (5, 15, 40 or 200: see Salvage); food stalls sell a tray meal for 6; vending machines take one Almond Water for a snack or a drink.
- The machines, counters, doors and windows cannot be broken. Dead machines, bins and dead neon can (see Salvage).
- Ways in and out: a lone arcade at the end of a line of five red-lit windmills in Level 10, a purple-flickering alley wall in the city, a computer in The End, magenta tiles under the far Poolrooms' deep water, and the Hub's door marked 3999 lead in; STAFF ONLY doors (one in six opens, onto the Hub), the mini arcade's elevator (Level 0), the themed cabinets (played to the end, one way to the level on the marquee) and the pools' drains (Level 37) lead out.
