- Level 3999.1, the Neon Blackout: far out, whole blocks of the mall have gone dark behind a stretch of failing neon. Cold (14 °C), it drains you fast, and Smilers, Hound packs and Partygoers hunt there. Its prize cases and ticket piles are free for the taking. A rusted cabinet in a row of machines is not solid: walk into it and you are in the dark.

Level 188, the Courtyard of Windows. A dark courtyard of mossy lawns and a round wooden deck, walled in by a five-storey hotel with 160 small square windows, under a black sky. You come in through a window and climb down into the courtyard. The window you came in by still shows where you came from, and leads back. Other windows on the ground floor show other places, and lead there. Inside, grey corridors run round the courtyard past unnumbered rooms; the stairs are in the north-west corner, the lifts are dead and the lobby's front door is locked. The building cannot be broken.
- Never open a blind from inside a room: whoever does is taken, one way, always to the same place for that window; the window then shows it, and the room's door stays shut for three days.
- If someone is standing in a lit window, waving, count which room it is and stay out. Within two blocks an arm comes out of the glass, and six seconds at the glass is death (see What Lives Here). They move to other windows every night.
- The rooms are warm (21 °C) and steady you a little: shut a room's door behind you and nothing comes in, unless someone was waving in its window. The courtyard is cold (8 °C) and drains you, the roof more.
- Clothes, cloth, beds and a little food (see Salvage). A fire exit on each upper floor leads out, each somewhere different, and the iron ring in the deck opens onto a long fall into the water of Level 37.
guide-bridge-knapping: In the Backrooms: there are no stones lying about in the Lobby, and flint is a Level 1 find: Level 1's crates hold it and its broken concrete has flint, chert, andesite and granite lying loose (a Lobby supply box holds one only about one time in twenty); Level 8's cave floors have stones too, and the ground under every floor holds flint as any world does. Knapping itself is unchanged. Until you have two flints, a glass shiv or an improvised scraper is your knife, and for wallpaper and carpet it stays the better one: see Salvage.
guide-bridge-clayforming: In the Backrooms: clay is the first thing you have to travel for. The nearest is the flooded tunnel under Level 3 (down a manhole; cold, and it drains your stability badly), then the beds of Level 10's ponds, rare pockets in Level 8's rock, and above all Level 94, whose hills are modelling clay under a skin of turf (about 3 clay a block, blue clay a little way down). The potted plants of Levels 4 and 5 give a slow trickle without the trip: their pottery shards, pounded to grit with a stone and worked into soil, make about one clay for every four plants (see Salvage). Clay forming itself is unchanged. Fire clay, for fire bricks, the bloomery and the kilns, lies only in Level 94, in pale seams three to seven blocks under the turf: see the Progression Guide.
guide-bridge-mealcooking: In the Backrooms: the pot and the bowls want clay (see above), and the firepit wants firewood, which is scarce in the first levels (rotten wood, planks, Level 7's driftwood, then the real trees of Levels 9 to 11 and 94). Water for a bucket is in the flooded rooms of Level 0, the tunnel under Level 3, the Poolrooms, Level 7's sea, Level 10's ponds and the city's fountains. Ingredients: fridges, pantries and crates give vegetables, fruit, cheese and flour; Level 7 fish; Level 9 game and berries; Level 10 crops, eggs, milk and honey. Cooking itself is unchanged.
guide-bridge-charcoalburning: In the Backrooms: charcoal is also found ready-made in Level 1's crates and Level 9's barbecue grills, and coal lies heaped by Level 3's generators and in Level 5's boiler halls, so you may not need a pit at all. If you do, nothing the Backrooms are built of burns, so any wall or floor of the building will seal a pit; but digging one into a floor takes a copper pickaxe (concrete and floor slabs are as hard as rock), unless you dig into the soil of Levels 9 or 10 or the clay of Level 94, or wall a corner with rubble masonry. The firewood is the hard part: see the Progression Guide.
guide-bridge-farming: In the Backrooms: it never rains, so moisture comes only from water within 3 blocks of the farmland or a watering can. Crops grow without sunlight under a working ceiling light, at about six tenths of the daylight pace (nothing grows under a dead one, and little in the cold of a blackout zone), so you can farm at home in the Lobby. Soil comes from potted plants (Levels 4 and 5), the lawns of Levels 9, 10 and 11, and Level 94's turf; the ground under the floors has none. Level 10's old fields are exhausted and never regrow: harvest them, then plant in fresh soil. Seeds: seed packets (tool shelves in Level 9's garages and sheds, now and then a supply box), seed sacks (Level 9's sheds, Level 10's barns), wanderers (flax, cabbage), and the harvest itself. See Home and Expeditions.
guide-bridge-foodpreservation: In the Backrooms: there are no seasons, so spoilage runs at the pace of the room you are in, all year. Any fully enclosed room counts as a cellar (concrete walls cool it; drywall does not), and Level 0's blackout zones are cold and damp (10 °C), so a chest there keeps food more than twice as long as the Lobby proper. Salt for pickling comes from kitchen cupboards or Level 8's halite ground in a quern; crocks and vessels from clay; wax from Level 10's skeps. See Food, Heat and Cold.
guide-bridge-animalhusbandry: In the Backrooms: livestock lives only in Level 10's paddocks: hens and a rooster, pigs, mouflon sheep and goats, a few at a time, with populated bee skeps by the farmhouses. Hares are in Level 9's gardens. Fences, troughs and henboxes are built from planks and sticks as usual; milk comes from the ewes and nannies. Nothing hostile closes in on the fields of Level 10, so a farm there is possible, but you still only wake up in Level 0.
guide-bridge-panning: In the Backrooms: there is almost nothing to pan. No sand or gravel lies under the floors; the only gravel is the surface of Level 8's road and the park paths of the city, and the muddy gravel of the pond beds will not pan. The one place with sand to pan is the floor of Level 7's sea (worlds made from 0.514.0), and a few of Level 10's ponds have a little. Copper comes far more easily from salvage: see the Progression Guide.
guide-bridge-smelting: In the Backrooms: the crucible and moulds need clay (Level 3's tunnel, Level 10's ponds, Level 94), and the heat needs coal (heaped by Level 3's generators and in Level 5's boiler halls) or charcoal (crates, grills, or your own pit). Copper comes as bits from cable spools, machine cabinets, stacked pipes, fans and wrecked cars rather than from ore: 20 metal bits = 1 ingot, and 10 scrap wire or 10 circuit boards melt to a copper ingot too. Ore proper is in Level 8 and in the ground under the floors. Tongs are made as usual. Iron ore needs a bloomery, and the bloomery needs fire bricks: the fire clay for them is in Level 94, and nowhere else, and the mortar to lay them wants sand: it lies on the floor of Level 7's sea, with a little in some of Level 10's ponds (worlds made from 0.514.0).
guide-bridge-smithing: In the Backrooms: a copper hammer sometimes turns up in a toolbox (Level 1, garages, hardware stores), or cast one; the anvil takes 9 ingots of copper or bronze; the forge is built as usual. Smithing itself is unchanged. Bronze comes from Level 8's tin, zinc, bismuth and gold with copper from salvage; iron needs a bloomery, whose fire clay comes only from Level 94.
guide-bridge-prospecting: In the Backrooms: the ground under every floor is an ordinary world's, 8 blocks of concrete down, with the Backrooms' floor at its sea level, and the prospecting pick reads it as usual (density mode only: node search is off). It does not read Level 8's own rock, whose ore is laid open on the cave walls and floors and needs no prospecting. Do not dig under Level 10 (the worms) and mind that Level 94's ground is clay, then rock.
guide-bridge-armor: In the Backrooms: improvised armour is sticks and twine as usual; leather comes from the hides of Hounds, Skin-Stealers, rats and Level 9's wildlife; wanderers sell sewn linen armour; iron and steel wait on a bloomery, whose fire clay is in Level 94 and nowhere else. From Level 6 down, what hunts you hits through one more grade of armour than it would nearer the Lobby, and in Level ! armour's weight slows you with a horde at your back. A party hat and a red balloon are the only armour that works in Level Fun.
guide-bridge-mechanicalpower: In the Backrooms: windmills turn only under an open sky, so only on Levels 9, 10, 11 and 94. There is no flowing water anywhere for a water wheel. Level 10's barns have a quern already, and Level 8's hard rock makes another. The helve hammer, pulverizer and grinding wheel work as usual once you have a windmill up on the open-sky levels.
guide-bridge-steelmaking: In the Backrooms: refractory bricks need fire clay, and the only fire clay in the Backrooms is in the seams under Level 94's hills, three to seven blocks down. A cementation furnace wants some 65 bricks, so plan several trips with bags; the iron and the coal come from Level 8. The bricks are laid in mortar (slaked lime and sand): sand lies thick on the floor of Level 7's sea, so plan a dive, and a few of Level 10's ponds have a little on the bed (worlds made from 0.514.0). Everything else is as usual.
guide-bridge-cokeoven: In the Backrooms: the coke oven is built of refractory bricks, whose fire clay comes only from the seams under Level 94's hills and whose mortar wants sand, from the floor of Level 7's sea (or, a little, some of Level 10's ponds; worlds made from 0.514.0). Coal itself is plentiful: Level 3's generators, Level 5's boilers and Level 8's seams.
guide-bridge-weather: In the Backrooms: there is no weather. It never rains or snows anywhere, there are no seasons, and each level keeps its own temperature all year (see Food, Heat and Cold). The open-sky levels have wind for windmills. The weather here is the Reality Shift: see Reality Stability.
guide-bridge-stonelayers: In the Backrooms: these rules hold for the ground under the floors (8 blocks of concrete down), which is an ordinary world's. Level 8's caves are the Backrooms' own rock, with limestone, chalk and halite among its strata and its ore laid open on the walls, and the ground proper begins far below it.
guide-bridge-cheese: In the Backrooms: milk comes from the ewes and nannies of Level 10's paddocks, pickled vegetables from Level 10's crops, salt from Level 8's halite or a kitchen cupboard, linen from hotel beds, and wax from Level 10's skeps. Cheese itself is made as usual. Ready-made cheese sits in the fridges of Levels 4 and 9, the city and Level 94.
guide-bridge-quenching: In the Backrooms: quenching works as usual wherever there is water (the flooded rooms of Level 0, the tunnel under Level 3, the Poolrooms, the ponds of Level 10). Copper and bronze take no quench, so this page matters once you have a bloomery (its fire clay is in Level 94) and iron from Level 8.
guide-bridge-fruittrees: In the Backrooms: there are no fruit trees. Fruit comes from fridges (Levels 4 and 9, the city, Level 94's iceboxes) and from the berry bushes gone wild in Level 9's gardens and along Level 10's fields. The trees of Levels 9, 10, 11 and 94 are oak, birch and maple, for wood.
guide-bridge-alcohol: In the Backrooms: barrels want boards (a saw, so copper); fruit comes from fridges and Level 9's berries, honey from Level 10's skeps, and flour from Level 10's grain ground in the barns' quern. The rest is as usual.
guide-bridge-dyemaking: In the Backrooms: flowers grow on the open-sky levels (9, 10, 11 and 94), and a pulverizer needs a windmill, which turns only there. Cloth itself is plentiful: sofas, chairs, suitcases and bedrolls give it, and so do Level 188's wardrobes. Clothes ready-made are in Level 5's wardrobes, Level 9's dressers and the city's stores.
guide-bridge-groundstorage: In the Backrooms: ground storage works as usual, and matters more, because a chest needs 8 planks from Level 1 and a basket needs Level 10's cattails. Lean your tools on the wall of your home in the Lobby until then.
guide-bridge-leathermaking: In the Backrooms: hides come from Death Rats (small), Hounds (medium), Skin-Stealers (large), Level 9's hares, foxes and raccoons, and Level 10's livestock. Limewater needs lime: Level 8's limestone and chalk, or the seashells of Level 7's islands, ground in a quern. Tannin needs oak, and about half the trees of Levels 9, 10, 11 and 94 are oak. Barrels need a saw. The steps are as usual.
guide-bridge-greenhouse: In the Backrooms: a greenhouse needs sky, so only the open-sky levels (9, 10, 11, 94) could hold one, and the glass is the work: glass shards from the Backrooms' lights are not glass blocks, so glass is made in a bloomery (fire clay from Level 94) from Level 8's quartz. Under a ceiling, a working light grows crops without any greenhouse: see farming.
guide-bridge-beehivekiln: In the Backrooms: the beehive kiln is built of refractory or fire bricks, whose fire clay comes only from the seams under Level 94's hills. The pit kiln fires everything you need until then.
guide-bridge-shipbuilding: In the Backrooms: the only sea is Level 7's, under a concrete ceiling (in worlds made from 0.514.0 a high one, thirty-six blocks over the water; before, only a few blocks above it), and nobody has yet found whether a sailboat fits under it. The raft from a waterlogged crate is the Backrooms' boat. Logs and boards exist (the trees of Levels 9 to 11 and 94, a saw), and rope comes from crates and toolboxes.
guide-bridge-mountableanimals: In the Backrooms: there are no elk and no mounts. Nobody rides here; the moving walkways of Level 3999 are the nearest thing.
guide-bridge-fishing: In the Backrooms: the fish are in Level 7's sea, and they are the sea's own kinds. Fishing poles turn up in the waterlogged crates on its bottom and in lost backpacks, or are made as usual. Worms for bait come from a worm grunter in the soil of Levels 9 or 10 (or Level 94's turf); meat and small fish work as bait too.
tutorial-backrooms-1: Use {0} {1} {2} {3} to move around and your mouse to look around. {4} jumps and {5} sneaks. Hold {6} and {0} to sprint, but not here: in the Backrooms, running is heard.
tutorial-backrooms-2: There is a wanderer's note in your pocket. With it in your hand, <icon>rightmousebutton</icon> to read it: it marks the nearest unopened supply box on your map. Every note you read is kept in your journal; press {0} to open it.
tutorial-backrooms-2-nowaypoints: There is a wanderer's note in your pocket. With it in your hand, <icon>rightmousebutton</icon> to read it: it tells you which way the nearest unopened supply box lies, and how many paces. Every note you read is kept in your journal, directions and all; press {0} to open it.
tutorial-backrooms-3: Two <itemstack type="block">backrooms:supplybox</itemstack> supply boxes stand beside you. Break one (hold <icon>leftmousebutton</icon>) and pick up what falls out: {0} more thing(s) to collect. A box with its lid taped down holds food; a torn one holds scraps.
tutorial-backrooms-4: Break a dead backrooms:fluorescentlight-off light fixture out of the ceiling for {0} backrooms:glassshard glass shard. Bare hands will do.
tutorial-backrooms-5: With the shard in your hand, rightmousebutton the yellow wallpaper to cut {0} backrooms:wallpaperstrip wallpaper strip. A bare shard snaps one time in four, so cut carefully.
tutorial-backrooms-6: Now rightmousebutton the carpet for {0} backrooms:carpetfibre carpet fibre. Dry carpet cuts; the soaked carpet of the dark zones does not.
tutorial-backrooms-7: Craft a backrooms:glassshiv glass shiv in your crafting grid (open your inventory with inventorydialog): a glass shard, a wallpaper strip and a carpet fibre. It is a knife, and it does not snap.
tutorial-backrooms-8: Bags next. With the shiv, cut {0} more <itemstack type="item">backrooms:carpetfibre</itemstack> carpet fibres from the carpet. It cuts cleanly: two fibres a block.
tutorial-backrooms-10: Craft a backrooms:carpetbag carpet bag: 5 carpet fibres and the twine. Put it in one of the 4 bag slots on the right of your inventory. You will want four of them, which is 32 carpet fibres.
tutorial-backrooms-11: Craft an backrooms:scraper improvised scraper: a backrooms:metalbracket metal bracket, a wallpaper strip and 2 carpet fibres. Brackets fall now and then from dead lights, ceiling tiles and supply boxes. Like the shiv it cuts two strips or fibres a block, and it lasts three times as long.
tutorial-backrooms-12: Tinder: craft {0} drygrass dry grass from 2 wallpaper strips. The Lobby has almost no firewood, and no flint either: dry grass and sticks are what fire starts with here.
tutorial-backrooms-13: Craft a <itemstack type="block">torch-basic-extinct-up</itemstack> torch: 2 dry grass above a stick. Sticks come from supply boxes, from rotten wood out of broken ceiling tiles, and now and then from a broken wall. Light it at a fire; a lit torch keeps things back where a candle only lights the dark.
tutorial-backrooms-14: Open the map with {0}. It shows only what you have seen, and remembers it. 'Where I woke up' is your home: you will wake there whenever you die, wherever you are.
tutorial-backrooms-15: That is the Lobby's whole toolkit. Stone tools wait for Level 1: flint is rare in the Lobby's boxes, but Level 1's crates hold it and its concrete floors have flint and stones lying loose; then knap a knife and an axe. Fire, food, the way to Level 1, the gear by your health and what lives in the dark are all in the handbook: press {0} and read the Starter Guide. Good luck, and don't run.
tutorial-backrooms-14-nowaypoints: Open the map with {0}. It shows only what you have seen, and remembers it, but in this world it marks nothing for you: <icon>rightmousebutton</icon> on it to add waypoints of your own. Where you woke up is your home: you will wake there whenever you die, wherever you are.
tutorial-backrooms-14-nomap: There is no map in this world: you find your way or you don't. Where you woke up is your home: you will wake there whenever you die, wherever you are, so learn the way back to it. A note gives a direction and a number of paces, and your journal ({0}) keeps them. Chalk arrows on the walls point to the ways through; leave your own with backrooms:chalk surveyor's chalk, from crumbled ceiling tiles.
tutorial-backrooms-started: Backrooms: First Steps is on screen. Hide it with .tutorial hud; find it again under Tutorials in the handbook (H).

note-l7-7:
A buoy out over deep water, a rope ladder hanging from it all the way down: under it a room on the seabed, its light still on, air trapped under its roof. Climb down, swim in under it, come up through the hatch and breathe. There's a chest in each, and the deeper the room the better what's in it. The deep ones are where the big thing circles.
— Dez
run-trip: You trip! Jump the junk on the floor at a sprint, or walk over it.
deadcreature-beast: Taken by the Beast of Level 5
beast-greet-1: A gentleman in a black fur suit stands where nobody stood a moment ago. "Ah, there you are. Let us strike a deal, you and I."
beast-greet-2: Out of the flames steps a gentleman in a black fur suit, and bows. "You need never be afraid again. Shake my hand."
beast-greet-3: A tall figure in a furred black suit holds out a clawed hand. "Welcome to my hotel. A small favour, and all your fear is gone."
beast-collect: "Time is up." A gentleman in a black fur suit is waiting for you. "I have come for what is mine."
beast-doubt: "Why are you doubting me?" His suit opens like wings.
beast-deal: You shake his hand. Warmth floods through you: you are whole, fed, and not afraid. "Splendid. I shall come for what is mine in three days."
beast-shocked: You hold his gaze. He stands as if struck, and for a few seconds nothing in the hotel moves. Run.
beast-free: Your soul is your own again.
beast-taken: The Beast of Level 5 has collected what you owed him.
beast-reprieve: You got away. He will come again for what is his.
blockdesc-mothhiveheart: Resin walled round columns of pale larvae, at the heart of a Deathmoth hive. Breaking it brings every female near, and more after them.
blockdesc-clumpremnant: What is left of a Clump: a patch of flesh on the floor. Left alone, it grows a new one in about a day. Fire ends it.
clumpremnant-hoursleft: Grows a new Clump in about {0} hours
itemdesc-mothquill: A hollow quill, a hand's length, pale with a dark tip, shed by a larva. Combine it with a spear in the crafting grid to coat the spear in venom (three hits), or with eight arrows to coat them (one hit each).
itemdesc-spidersilk: A skein of grey-white silk, strong and very fine. Two make a flax twine in the crafting grid.
itemdesc-clumpsinew: A coil of dried pale sinew. It does for string: bows and slings can be made with it in place of twine or rope, and four make a rope.
itemdesc-mothjelly: A lump of amber jelly from a Deathmoth hive. Right-click to set it down: for a minute it draws every male Deathmoth and Death Rat within twenty-four blocks to it.
venom-info: The next {0} hits poison what they wound: 1 damage every 2 seconds for 6 seconds.
venom-info-arrow: Poisons what it wounds: 1 damage every 2 seconds for 6 seconds.
